domain_label: Movie Studio Director — Production Operations: Asset Registry, Provenance, Checklist and Owner Escalation
purpose: A method for the operational backbone of an AI reel studio: naming and versioning every asset (prompts, keyframes, clips, Souls, Reference Elements), designing the persona-asset registry from a workspace that is currently empty, recording per-clip provenance (which model, params, prompt version produced each kept clip), running the per-reel checklist from brief to posted, and escalating to the owner on credit-spend thresholds, likeness/policy flags, identity drift beyond tolerance, or any real-person identifiability — every platform capability sourced from the live Higgsfield MCP surface enumeration of 2026-07-03, never from memory.

the workspace persona surfaces are empty as of the enumeration — show_characters and show_reference_elements both returned zero items — so the persona-asset registry is designed from zero, not migrated

per-generation credit costs, Soul-training credit cost, and rate limits are all [UNKNOWN] on the read surface; the surface's own sanctioned probe is get_cost:true on a generate_* call, so every cost figure in this KB is a knob to preflight, never a stated price

Training credit cost [UNKNOWN].

A <<<element_id>>> marker embedded in a generate_image/generate_video prompt referencing a Reference Element (instant, no training; category character|environment|prop); multiple tokens per prompt are allowed, making Elements the surface-designated path for two-persona shots; Elements are NOT usable with Soul models [FACT — live tool descriptions 2026-07-03].

Any id minted by Higgsfield rather than the studio: media_id (from media_confirm), job_id (from a generation), soul_id, element_id. Stored as foreign keys on ledger rows; generate_* media value accepts a media_id or a prior job_id, never a URL [FACT — generate_* schemas].

Mandatory before any untested model x resolution x duration cell because per-generation prices are [UNKNOWN] on the read surface.

An immutable, id-carrying snapshot of exact prompt text (including embedded element tokens). Any edit mints a new version id; generations reference the version id, so every kept clip's wording is reconstructable and A/B results stay attributable.

The provenance linkage of a stitched reel: clip N's end_image handle feeds clip N+1's start_image (structurally supported because media value accepts a prior generation's job_id [FACT — generate_video schema]); each seam row records the transition type plus both frame handles, so a re-roll upstream marks downstream clips stale instead of silently breaking the stitch.

A persona's face geometry, eye color, hair or wardrobe changing across frames or shots — an industry-named AI-video failure mode [FACT — via search excerpts in the realism research]. Checked as the identity-lock rubric item against the persona reference sheet at every QC checkpoint; the quantitative fidelity gap between Souls and Elements is [UNKNOWN] until A/B generation runs.

The standing policy that any real-person identifiability — a generated face resembling an identifiable real individual, or a request to evoke one — halts the affected work and escalates to the owner. No technique for approximating a specific real person while obscuring the face is recorded anywhere in this system; the lane is closed, not narrow.

A per-model, per-shot-type record of failure classes, keep-rate, and the learned color trim preset (each model batch arrives with its own color signature, so a per-model trim nudge toward the house target is maintained before hero-clip matching — process design from the editing research, actual signatures [UNKNOWN until generation runs]).

What an owner escalation must contain: the trigger, the ledger rows evidencing it (asset ids, provenance, spend), the halted-or-continuing state of affected work, and the specific decision requested — so the owner rules on evidence, not on a summary.

nodes.definition: Fix the naming and versioning convention before anything is generated, because it keys every other record. Local ids are deterministic and human-parseable, embedding reel, shot/seam, asset role and version — e.g. a still keyframe for reel 003, shot 02, end-frame role, version 4 is one string that sorts and greps — covering all five asset classes: prompts, keyframes (start/end stills), clips, Souls and Reference Elements, plus reels themselves. Versions are monotone integers minted on any change; nothing is edited in place. Platform-minted handles (media_id, job_id, soul_id, element_id) are never used as local keys and never renamed — they are foreign keys carried on the row (their mechanics are the platform-handle node). The scheme is designed from zero honestly: no naming convention exists in the workspace yet, so this node is a design commitment [ESTIMATE — standard asset-management practice applied to this pipeline; the asset classes themselves are FACT from the live surface].

nodes.definition: Treat every prompt as an immutable versioned artifact. A prompt row carries: version id (per the naming grammar), exact text including embedded <<<element_id>>> tokens, the shot/seam it serves, and its lineage (which version it derives from and why — a QC failure class, a transition change, a model swap). Any edit mints a new version; the old version stays because kept clips reference it. Every generation call records the prompt version id it used, which is what makes A/B results attributable: when two batches differ, the ledger can prove whether the prompt, the model, or the params moved. This discipline is a design commitment [ESTIMATE — version-control practice applied to prompt assets], but the payload it protects is factual: prompts carry the element tokens and craft vocabulary that the platform surfaces do not archive with the job.

nodes.definition: Record the stitched reel's seam structure as first-class provenance. The platform structurally supports chaining: a generate_video media value accepts a prior generation's job_id, so clip N's end frame can seed clip N+1's start frame [FACT — generate_video schema]. Each seam row records: the transition type chosen for that seam (the shot-pipeline KB chooses it; this KB records it), the end-keyframe handle of clip N, the start-keyframe handle of clip N+1, whether the pair was chained by job_id or generated as separate stills, and the QC match verdict on the pair. The chain is what makes re-rolls safe: when any upstream clip or keyframe is re-rolled, every downstream row that references its handles is automatically marked STALE, forcing a deliberate re-link or regeneration instead of a silently broken stitch. Without seam rows, a reel is just a folder of clips and the most expensive property of the format — engineered continuity — is untracked.

nodes.definition: Enforce the closed likeness lane. Trigger conditions: a generated persona or any output resembles an identifiable real individual; a brief, comment, or internal suggestion asks to evoke a specific real person (by name, by 'like that actress', by supplying a real person's photo as a reference); or a reference-image set for a Soul/Element contains a real identifiable person without documented consent lineage. What this node deliberately does NOT contain, by standing policy: any technique for approximating a real person's likeness while obscuring or altering the face — the lane is closed, and 'closed' means no workaround guidance exists anywhere in the system, not that a clever framing is pending approval. The gate applies from the earliest cheap point: the persona reference sheets at registry bootstrap are the first likeness review, before any credits are spent, and every QC checkpoint re-checks because generation is stochastic and resemblance can emerge unprompted.

nodes.definition: Compose the escalation system: WHAT goes to the owner, with what evidence, and which trigger wins. Four trigger families: (1) credit-spend — any threshold from the accounting node fires (first Soul training, oversized single call, reel cap breach, balance floor; thresholds [ESTIMATE] until ratified); (2) likeness/policy — any likeness-gate flag, carrying the psych-boundary framing that audience 'this is AI' accusations will happen even on clean content (the research's Dunning-Kruger finding), so POLICY flags escalate but mere accusation-comments do not; (3) identity drift beyond tolerance with the retrain decision attached; (4) any real-person identifiability, which is family 2's hard core. Precedence when several fire: likeness/identifiability outranks everything and halts rather than queues; drift-beyond-tolerance halts its lineage; credit triggers pause new spend but let QC and post on already-generated assets continue. Every escalation is a packet — trigger, ledger-row evidence, halted/continuing state, specific decision requested — and every owner ruling is written back as a ledger event so the same question is not re-escalated. Escalation is a designed interface, not an apology: the system's autonomy is defined by exactly these boundaries.

seam-bearing slots pass chained handles per the seam rows, on both-frames models
post consumes only kept, provenance-complete clips the video stage closes
per-model trim presets from the failure ledger apply before hero-clip matching
release packages the exported master and its recorded grade lineage
drift detection rides the identity-lock item at the checkpoints the gate node places
the drift baseline is the Soul's recorded training-image set, a lifecycle artifact
the first likeness review runs on the reference sheets the bootstrap plan authors
the credit trigger family fires on the thresholds the accounting node defines
likeness flags are the matrix's highest-precedence input
beyond-tolerance drift escalates with the retrain decision attached
the gates demand re-rolls until clean while the accounting caps spend — quality appetite versus budget
edges.resolution_rule: below the reel cap and thresholds, the QC gate wins and re-rolls run; at a threshold the credit trigger fires and the owner decides — the system never silently relaxes a gate to save credits, and never silently overspends to satisfy one

edges.why_related: Souls promise identity fidelity but reach only two image models with one Soul per generation; Elements reach most models and multi-persona shots but with unproven fidelity
edges.resolution_rule: route solo hero stills through Souls on soul_2/soul_cinematic and all two-persona or non-Soul-model shots through Elements; revisit the split when the fidelity A/B lands, and never force a two-Soul shot the surface forbids

edges.why_related: the ledger argues for exploiting the known-best model per shot type while the owner's try-different directive argues for exploration
edges.resolution_rule: repeat shot types default to the ledger winner; declared A/B exploration is reserved for new shot types, post-model-update revalidation, or a ledger keep-rate below par — exploration is a budgeted decision, not a habit

edges.why_related: posting momentum and owner enthusiasm push toward publishing while an open likeness flag demands a halt
edges.resolution_rule: the likeness flag always wins: nothing posts while any flag on any constituent asset is open, whatever the schedule cost — the closed lane admits no posting-deadline exception

edges.why_related: frozen prompt versions serve attribution while batch iteration wants mid-flight wording tweaks
edges.resolution_rule: any wording change mints a new version id before the call — the tweak is allowed, the untracked tweak is not; batches reference frozen versions so A/B results stay attributable

edges.why_related: every batch's keep/kill outcomes and failure classes flow back into the per-model ledger that steers the next batch
QC failure classes that implicate wording drive new prompt versions, closing the quality-to-prompt loop
an open escalation on any constituent asset blocks the release gate until the owner rules

conflict_axes.name: qc_perfection_vs_credit_budget
conflict_axes.description: Re-rolling until every rubric item is clean burns credits without bound, while hard caps tempt shipping visible tells; with per-generation prices [UNKNOWN] the tension cannot be priced away upfront.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: QC wins below thresholds; a tripped threshold escalates rather than silently relaxing either side

conflict_axes.name: soul_fidelity_vs_element_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: Souls are the identity-faithful path but reach two image models with one Soul per generation; Elements reach the broad catalog and two-persona shots with an unproven fidelity gap.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: dual-track per persona (one Soul plus one Element) and let the first fidelity A/B set the production split

conflict_axes.name: explore_models_vs_exploit_ledger
conflict_axes.description: The owner's try-different directive rewards exploration while the failure ledger's whole value is exploiting accumulated winners.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: exploit on repeat shot types, explore as a budgeted declared decision on new types or after model updates

conflict_axes.name: iteration_speed_vs_provenance_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Fast creative iteration wants to tweak and re-fire; complete provenance wants every call versioned, preflighted and rowed before it runs.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make logging cheap (templates, write-at-submit) rather than optional; the untracked tweak, not the tweak, is the violation

conflict_axes.name: posting_cadence_vs_policy_hold
conflict_axes.description: Feed momentum and owner enthusiasm reward shipping on schedule, while open likeness flags, drift quarantines, or escalations demand holds of unpredictable length.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: policy holds always win; protect cadence by keeping a cleared-reel buffer, not by shortening reviews

conflict_axes.name: local_ledger_vs_platform_surfaces
conflict_axes.description: Duplicating bookkeeping locally costs discipline, but the platform's history surfaces have [UNKNOWN] retention/query semantics and cannot hold prompt versions or QC verdicts.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: local ledger is canonical; platform surfaces are reconciliation inputs whose semantics get documented as they are exercised

conflict_axes.name: registry_upfront_design_vs_first_output_speed
conflict_axes.description: Designing registry rows, naming and caps before generating delays the first visible reel, which owner enthusiasm punishes.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bootstrap is one session's work and every skipped row is paid back with interest as orphaned lineage; show the owner the plan as the first deliverable

conflict_axes.name: autonomy_vs_owner_interrupts
conflict_axes.description: Tight escalation triggers keep the owner in control but interrupt them constantly; loose triggers preserve flow but let spend or policy risk run unsupervised.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: escalate on the four families only, batch non-urgent packets, write rulings back so the same question never re-escalates

conflict_axes.name: asset_reuse_vs_fresh_generation
conflict_axes.description: Reusing archived keyframes, Souls and prompt versions compounds their value and consistency, but stale assets can lock in an early look or a drifted baseline.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reuse anything whose QC verdict and baseline still stand; a retrain or house-look change stales the affected archive explicitly rather than by decay

edge_cases.description: The catalog carries duplicate model ids (soul_2 and soul_v2, identical schemas), and per-model statistics split across the two spellings
edge_cases.mitigation: canonicalize to soul_2 in the ledger with soul_v2 recorded as alias; merge any split history on discovery

edge_cases.description: An Elements-routed generation may execute on a different engine than the id suggests (nano_banana_2 displays as 'Nano Banana Pro'; nano_banana_flash is catalog-absent), corrupting attribution
edge_cases.trigger: the first element-token batch runs before routing is resolved
edge_cases.mitigation: instrument the first element-routed generation to record requested vs reported ids and hold per-model conclusions on element batches until routing is resolved

edge_cases.description: Soul training cost is [UNKNOWN] and training cannot be get_cost-preflighted the way generate_* calls can, so the first training is a blind spend
edge_cases.trigger: the bootstrap plan reaches its first Soul training
edge_cases.mitigation: escalate before the first training with the balance snapshot; record the observed cost as the cached price for future trainings

edge_cases.description: A persona generation is requested while the registry is still empty (the workspace's actual state), leaving identity lineage nowhere to attach
edge_cases.trigger: owner enthusiasm demands output before bootstrap completes
edge_cases.mitigation: intake blocks on unresolved registry refs; offer the owner the bootstrap plan plus a non-persona test reel as the immediate deliverable

edge_cases.description: A generation job fails after its provenance row was opened, or a job_id later fails to resolve, leaving orphan rows
edge_cases.trigger: job failure, retention expiry, or workspace switch between submit and reconcile
edge_cases.mitigation: reconcile open rows against job_display after every batch; orphaned rows move to a failed state with the error recorded, never deleted

edge_cases.description: A two-persona shot is planned with two soul_ids, which the surface forbids (ONE soul_id per generation)
edge_cases.trigger: a shot plan treats Souls as freely combinable
edge_cases.mitigation: route all two-persona shots through multiple element tokens on an element-compatible model; the intake check catches the plan before spend

edge_cases.description: Identity drift is first noticed at the post-edit phone check, after still, video and grading spend are already sunk
edge_cases.trigger: subtle per-clip drift accumulates across the reel below single-clip thresholds
edge_cases.mitigation: enforce the identity-lock item at checkpoint 1 against the reference sheet, and add a cross-clip side-by-side review before assembly on persona-heavy reels

edge_cases.description: A kept clip is discovered without a prompt version (an untracked manual tweak produced it), making its look unreproducible
edge_cases.trigger: batch momentum bypassed the version-minting rule
edge_cases.mitigation: quarantine the clip; backfill the version from call logs if recoverable, else regenerate from the nearest recorded version before the clip anchors further work

edge_cases.description: The credit balance drops more than the ledger's recorded spend explains
edge_cases.trigger: parallel workspace activity, plan renewal, or an unrecorded call
edge_cases.mitigation: reconcile against the transactions surface, freeze new spend until the gap is explained, and escalate with the discrepancy packet if it is not

edge_cases.description: A generated persona turns out to resemble an identifiable real person even though nothing in the prompt asked for it
edge_cases.trigger: stochastic generation lands near a real face; a comment or reviewer names the person
edge_cases.mitigation: halt the lineage, flag all touched rows, escalate with the resemblance evidence; if already posted, the owner's ruling covers takedown — the closed lane offers no restyle-and-continue shortcut

edge_cases.description: An upstream clip is re-rolled after downstream clips were chained on its end_image job_id, silently invalidating the stitch
edge_cases.trigger: a late QC failure or owner note forces a re-roll mid-assembly
edge_cases.mitigation: stale-marking fires on the re-roll and blocks assembly until every downstream seam is re-linked or regenerated

edge_cases.description: The wardrobe-module library is built out before the Souls-vs-Elements fidelity gap [UNKNOWN] is tested, and the chosen mechanism underperforms
edge_cases.trigger: registry enthusiasm outruns the scheduled first A/B
edge_cases.mitigation: cap the pre-A/B library at the minimum viable set (one wardrobe module per persona) and gate expansion on the recorded A/B verdict

workflow.action: Fix the naming grammar and stand up the production ledger
workflow.description: Author the local id grammar for all five asset classes plus reels, and open the append-only ledger keyed on it with platform handles as foreign keys
workflow.artifact: naming convention + empty ledger with row schema
workflow.gate: every asset class has an id form, versioning is monotone, and platform handles are foreign-key fields only

workflow.action: Author the persona-asset registry bootstrap plan
workflow.description: Design rows from the verified-empty workspace: one Soul plus one Element per persona, wardrobe as prop/character Elements, locations as environment Elements, each with reference-image lineage
workflow.gate: both personas have Soul and Element rows, wardrobe/location rows exist, and the likeness review of reference sheets is recorded

workflow.action: Create the identity assets and record their handles
workflow.description: Escalate the first (unknown-cost) Soul training, then train Souls and create Elements per the plan, writing soul_id/element_id and source-image handles to their rows
workflow.artifact: populated registry rows with platform handles
workflow.gate: each created asset's row carries its handle, source lineage and status; the training cost is cached; no creation ran without its row

workflow.action: Intake the reel brief into a tracked production spec
workflow.description: Mint the reel id, resolve slots and registry refs, set the spend cap, and declare escalation-sensitive flags
workflow.artifact: reel spec with slot list, cap and flags
workflow.gate: no unresolved registry refs, a cap is set, and likeness/new-Soul/untested-cost flags are explicit

workflow.action: Preflight every untested cost cell for the reel
workflow.description: Run get_cost:true on each new model x resolution x duration cell the plan touches and cache results in the ledger against the cap
workflow.artifact: priced cost table for the reel
workflow.gate: every planned call has a cached preflighted price and the summed plan fits the cap or has escalated

workflow.action: Generate and QC the keyframe stills, seam pairs as pairs
workflow.description: Produce start/end stills per slot on the correct identity path, run checkpoint 1, and match seam pairs on position/brightness/color/blur direction
workflow.artifact: promoted keyframe set with QC scores
workflow.gate: only checkpoint-1-passed stills and matched pairs are promoted; failures re-rolled at still prices

workflow.action: Run the video batches with full provenance
workflow.description: Call ledger-chosen models in-band with chained keyframes, opening provenance rows at submit and closing them at keep/kill with failure classes
workflow.artifact: kept clips with complete provenance rows
workflow.gate: every call preflighted where new, every output rowed, re-roll counts recorded, killed clips retained as evidence

workflow.action: Gate raw video at checkpoint 2 including identity lock
workflow.description: Score each clip on the rubric, enforce the single-2 and total>=4 re-roll rules, and check drift against the reference sheet
workflow.artifact: written QC verdicts on every provenance row
workflow.gate: no clip proceeds unscored; re-roll rules enforced; any beyond-tolerance drift quarantines and escalates

workflow.action: Assemble, match to the hero clip, and export the master
workflow.description: Beat-lock, apply per-model trims then hero matching then the house look, QC cut boundaries, export 1080x1920 and run the phone-screen checkpoint
workflow.artifact: graded master with grade lineage and boundary verdicts
workflow.gate: only kept clips assembled; boundary frames within the match window; phone-screen pass recorded

workflow.description: Record cover choice, post at highest quality, verify live playback and crops, and write the release row linking published output to provenance
workflow.artifact: release row with master hash and provenance links
workflow.gate: no open escalation/flag/quarantine on any constituent asset; verification checks pass; the row is complete

workflow.action: Sweep escalation triggers and update the ledgers
workflow.description: Close the reel by checking all four trigger families, sending any packets with ledger evidence, writing owner rulings back, and folding batch outcomes into the failure ledger
workflow.artifact: escalation packets and updated failure-ledger entries
workflow.gate: no unsent trigger, no unrecorded ruling, and the failure ledger reflects every batch

priority_rationale: The foundations (naming grammar, canonical ledger, prompt versioning, platform-handle semantics) come first because every registry row, provenance record and escalation packet is keyed on them; the registry trio (bootstrap plan, Soul lifecycle, Element lifecycle, collision guard) comes next because the workspace is verifiably empty and identity assets must exist with recorded lineage before any persona generation; the provenance layer (clip rows, seam chains, failure ledger, credit accounting) precedes the pipeline stages because rows are written AT generation time, not after; the pipeline stages (intake, QC gates, stills, video, post, release) then execute in cost order — cheapest failure first; and the governance nodes (likeness gate, drift tolerance, escalation matrix) bind across all stages, with the likeness closed lane outranking everything because its failures are the only irreversible ones.

dominance_rules.rule: A likeness/identifiability flag dominates every other consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: the lane is closed by policy and the harm is irreversible once posted
dominance_rules.trigger: any real-person resemblance, request, or consent-less reference surfaces at any stage
dominance_rules.action: halt the lineage, flag all touched rows, escalate with evidence; nothing on that lineage generates, polishes or posts until the owner rules

dominance_rules.rule: The registry bootstrap dominates the first persona generation
dominance_rules.rationale: the workspace is verifiably empty, and identity lineage generated before rows exist is orphaned from day one
dominance_rules.trigger: a persona generation is requested before its registry rows exist
dominance_rules.action: block at intake and deliver the bootstrap plan (or a non-persona test) instead

dominance_rules.rule: get_cost preflight dominates any untested-cost call
dominance_rules.rationale: every per-generation price is [UNKNOWN] on the read surface and the probe is free
dominance_rules.trigger: a call touches a model x resolution x duration cell with no cached price
dominance_rules.action: preflight, cache the price, then submit — or escalate if the price breaks the cap

dominance_rules.rule: Provenance completeness dominates keeping a clip
dominance_rules.rationale: an unreproducible clip cannot be regraded, re-rendered, audited or defended later
dominance_rules.trigger: a clip is about to be kept with any missing provenance field
dominance_rules.action: quarantine until backfilled from evidence or regenerate; incomplete rows never enter timelines

dominance_rules.rationale: polishing an ungated clip spends credits on output that may be re-rolled anyway
dominance_rules.trigger: an upscale or post operation is queued for a clip without a written checkpoint-2 verdict
dominance_rules.action: run the gate first; spend polish credits only on gated keeps

dominance_rules.rule: The credit threshold dominates re-roll appetite
dominance_rules.rationale: with prices unknown and the balance finite (1,010 at enumeration), unbounded quality-chasing is the likeliest silent failure
dominance_rules.trigger: re-roll counts or summed spend reach a threshold or the reel cap
dominance_rules.action: pause new spend, keep QC/post running on existing assets, and escalate with the spend packet

dominance_rules.rule: The reference-sheet baseline dominates adjacent-clip comparison for drift
dominance_rules.rationale: measuring drift clip-to-clip lets it ratchet; the training images are the fixed truth
dominance_rules.trigger: an identity-lock check is about to compare against the previous clip only
dominance_rules.action: compare against the Soul/Element source images recorded in the registry, then check accumulation at phone QC

dominance_rules.rule: Exact model id strings dominate display names everywhere in the ledger
dominance_rules.rationale: the surface's documented naming collisions make display names actively misleading
dominance_rules.trigger: any row, ledger entry or report is about to reference a model by display name
dominance_rules.action: record the exact id string, canonicalize known aliases, and instrument element-routed calls until routing resolves

dominance_rules.rule: The local ledger dominates platform history surfaces on any disagreement
dominance_rules.rationale: the platform surfaces have [UNKNOWN] semantics and cannot carry prompt versions or QC verdicts
dominance_rules.trigger: show_generations/transactions and the ledger disagree about an asset or a spend
dominance_rules.action: treat the ledger as canonical, investigate the gap, and record the resolution as a ledger event

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the naming grammar and ledger schema before the first generation call
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mass rename and lineage reconstruction across hundreds of assets once ad-hoc names collide

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write provenance at submit time, never retrospectively
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unreconstructable kept clips, because no platform surface archives prompt versions or QC verdicts to backfill from

anti_rework_rules.rule: QC stills and seam pairs before any video call
anti_rework_rules.prevents: paying video prices to discover composition, identity or pair-match failures that still prices would have caught

anti_rework_rules.rule: Preflight each new cost cell with get_cost before first use
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a single mispriced batch consuming a visible fraction of the 1,010-credit balance and forcing an emergency owner conversation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Create both personas' Elements before planning any two-persona shot
anti_rework_rules.prevents: replanning a reel mid-production around the one-Soul-per-generation limit discovered at generation time

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mint the prompt version before the batch, not after the keeper is found
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unattributable A/B results that force re-running the comparison to learn which wording won

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the identity-lock check at checkpoint 1 against the reference sheet
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sinking video, grading and assembly spend into a drifted persona caught only at the phone-screen pass

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record per-model failure classes and trim presets from the first batches onward
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-discovering each model's quirks and color signature on every subsequent reel

anti_rework_rules.rule: Review reference sheets for likeness before any Soul trains or Element is created
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retiring a trained persona and its whole archive because the resemblance was caught after production scaled

iteration_protocol.trigger: a likeness or real-person-identifiability flag fires anywhere in production
iteration_protocol.action: halt the lineage, flag all touched ledger rows, send the evidence packet, and record the owner's ruling as a ledger event before any affected work resumes

iteration_protocol.trigger: credit spend reaches a threshold, the reel cap, or an unexplained balance gap appears
iteration_protocol.action: pause new spend, reconcile against balance/transactions, and escalate with the spend packet; resume only under a recorded ruling

iteration_protocol.trigger: identity drift beyond tolerance is confirmed on any clip or accumulating across a reel
iteration_protocol.action: quarantine the lineage, diagnose Soul vs Element vs prompt, and escalate with the retrain/re-create decision; a retrain mints new rows and stales the old baseline's archive

iteration_protocol.trigger: the first Souls-vs-Elements fidelity A/B completes
iteration_protocol.action: record the verdict, set the production split between the two identity paths, and unlock or cap the wardrobe-library buildout accordingly

iteration_protocol.trigger: the first instrumented element-routed generation resolves (or deepens) the model-id routing question
iteration_protocol.action: update the collision guard's canonical map, and re-attribute or annotate any element-batch entries in the failure ledger

iteration_protocol.trigger: the failure ledger shows a repeated failure class or a keep-rate collapse for a model x shot-type cell
iteration_protocol.action: switch that shot type's default model, note the deprecation in the ledger, and re-run a budgeted A/B only if no cell performs

iteration_protocol.trigger: a provenance gap, orphan row, or ledger/platform mismatch is discovered in an audit or reconcile pass
iteration_protocol.action: quarantine affected assets, backfill from job_display/transactions evidence where possible, and patch the logging hole that produced the gap

iteration_protocol.trigger: a later surface enumeration changes the catalog (new models, resolved element-compatibility list, exercised history-surface semantics, or plan change)
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the affected registry and ledger schema checks, update cached constraints (both-frames list, duration bands, compatible models), and re-price impacted cost cells
